title: Moving to the senior citizens' building in the Bronx
summary: He moved in 1965 after a hip injury and hospital stay.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, we've come to the end of pretty much the main part of the interview, a lot of the chronology and your itinerary, who you played with and so forth. I would like to ask a couple of questions, however, one which we didn't touch on, and that is (except in the very beginning) your family, and your wife, and... You've lived here apparently... This is a senior citizens' building in the Bronx. How long have you been living here, and is it convenient to where you have to go to get to work sometimes?

I moved into the senior citizens' building in 1965. During '65...'64, that's when I got my leg hurt, my hip knocked out of place rather, and I was in the hospital, and I stayed in there, oh, I'd say about four or five weeks. I was all right. I wasn't all right, but they wanted to let me out after five weeks. So they kept me five more weeks before they had a place for me. They got me this place here. And one of the big head ladies down there, she got me into this place. I was the first one to move in here, in this building. That was 19-and... Well, after '65 or the first of '64, somewhere around there. And I've been here ever since.
Are there other musicians in this building, by the way?
